changes.planned: One human sky-repair worker with a stable silhouette and dark brass climbing harness.
changes.observed: One adult sky-repair worker remains visible as a dark segmented climbing silhouette with a long red cape; facial detail is indistinct at this distance.

changes.planned: Cold storm daylight from upper camera-left; amber fissure bounce on wet brass and oilcloth.
changes.observed: Soft cold-gray storm light exposes the steel tower and clouds. The vertical fissure and handheld amber light add warm edge illumination to the worker; the steel remains dull and weathered rather than glossy.

changes.planned: Worker ends swinging screen-right as the safety cable first becomes taut.
changes.observed: The worker ends suspended almost horizontally away from the tower with residual screen-right motion blur. The cable is taut toward the lower frame rather than the planned lower-left anchor, the cape trails screen-right, and physical contact with the tower has not resumed.

changes.planned: Worker stays left of the vertical sky fissure and moves screen-right on the tower exterior.
changes.observed: At the accepted endpoint the worker is fully screen-right of the bright vertical fissure and tower, not left of it. The tower occupies the left half of frame, open storm sky occupies the right, and the camera stays on the same exterior side.

changes.planned: The repair attempt begins, but the fissure widens and pulls the worker off the tower rib.
changes.observed: The fissure has opened and the worker has swung completely off the tower while remaining tethered. Recovery, renewed tower contact, and the repair itself remain unresolved.

changes.planned: Heavy red oilcloth cape with one triangular lower edge; compact amber repair torch in the right hand; steel safety cable anchored lower-left.
changes.observed: The red cape remains attached and trails away from the torso. An amber repair light remains visible in the hand nearest the tower. A thin safety cable exits the lower torso and continues out of frame; no equipment damage is clearly visible.
